$meta.procedure: Figma variables -> this file is synced by Claude via Figma MCP (see CLAUDE.md / ADR-0010). Then run `pnpm sync:tokens` to regenerate app/theme.css. Never edit app/theme.css by hand.

duration.$comment: Ticket #86: Figma carries no prototype reactions/transitionDuration on the Sidebar component set (or anywhere else in this file) — there is no Figma value to resolve here, only a codebase-picked default. See design/tokens.json's semantic.$comment and docs/open-questions.md#sidebar-motion-timing-unsourced.

easing.$comment: Ticket #86: same caveat as duration above — no Figma source. 'out' deliberately matches the standard ease-out cubic-bezier CSS already ships as its own default `ease-out` utility (see node_modules/tailwindcss/theme.css) so the curve itself is not a new invention, only its promotion to a named project token is.

semantic.$comment: A plain string ref is a light-only token (no dark variant yet). An object { light, dark } carries a dark-mode override. `pnpm sync:tokens` emits the dark refs into a `[data-theme="dark"] { ... }` block in app/theme.css — that attribute is what Ladle's Light/Dark toggle sets on <html> (see @ladle/react's init-side-effects.ts); it's also the hook the real app would use once it grows its own theme switch (not built yet, out of scope for #42). Dark values below are this round's addition (2026-07-20, ticket #42), scoped to the primitives Atom/Button actually uses — no Figma dark-mode frames exist to fetch, so these are derived by staying inside Tailwind's stock stone/red scale rather than inventing one-off hex. Not every token has a dark counterpart yet; that's a flagged gap for a future token-sync pass, not an oversight. TICKET #56 (2026-07-20, supersedes #52's state tier): Figma added a FOURTH state to Button/Default and redistributed the values. What #52 recorded as Hover is now Active (pressed); Hover took a milder new value; Selected no longer changes the background at all — it only darkens the text to `text`. The scale is therefore `role` / `role-hover` / `role-active`, and the `*-selected` colour tokens #52 added (surface-selected, surface-raised-selected, border-selected, priority-urgent-bg-selected) were REMOVED rather than left as dead names — Selected needs no background token. `surface-hover` changed from stone-300 (which had no consumer) to stone-50 and now backs Button/White's Hover; `surface-active` (stone-100) shares its primitive with `surface-muted` but is kept as a separate name because it is a distinct role — a state colour, not a static surface. TICKET #58 (2026-07-20): re-fetched Atom/Input-field (node 3705:4402) expecting it to have been re-bound onto Button's shared border/border-hover/border-active scale now that Figma redistributed a fourth state (Selected) onto it. It has NOT: Default matches Button's Default (stone-300, so it keeps reading the shared `border` token, no component-scoped token needed there), but Hover (stone-500) and the new Active (a value with no prior primitive, added this ticket as `stone-600`) are genuinely different pixels from Button/Outline's Hover (stone-400) and Active (stone-700) — confirmed by fetching both nodes side by side, not assumed. The good news: the #56-era bug (Hover darker than Active, backwards from Button) is gone — Hover (stone-500) is now correctly lighter than Active (stone-600), same direction as Button. So this is no longer a stale/unbound node; it is a deliberately distinct border ramp, kept under its own tokens rather than forced onto Button's. `border-input-focus` is renamed `border-input-active` (it reads Figma's actual `Active` state; the old name described this atom's `:focus-within` *interpretation* of that state, which still holds — see design/figma-map.json). `border-input-hover` keeps its stone-500 value unchanged. Now that this node carries the SAME four state names as Atom/Button, its CSS hooks follow the same semantics Button established in #56, so all four states are modelled: Hover -> `hover:`, Active -> `active:` (Figma's Active means 'being pressed', which is what CSS :active means), Selected -> `:focus-within`. Selected is the state whose sample shows a typed value (text stone-950) rather than the placeholder, i.e. the field has been engaged - which is exactly what :focus-within expresses, and it is a better fit than the pre-#58 reading that put :focus-within on Active. That mapping is still this atom's interpretation (Figma labels states, not CSS hooks) and stays flagged in design/figma-map.json for confirmation. `border-input-selected` (stone-400) backs it. Dark values remain this codebase's own pick (no Figma dark frames exist); the destructive hover/active pair still both resolve to red-950 in dark mode, i.e. those states are invisible there — a known, flagged gap, not an oversight. Figma MCP still returns resolved hex only, never variable names, so every semantic name here is derived from values, not read from Figma. TICKET #68 (2026-07-20): re-fetched Atom/Button (3623:4346) and Atom/Input-field (3705:4402) again, per the ticket's premise that the user re-authored Button/Outline's borders since #58. Confirmed, pixel-for-pixel, not assumed: three of the four states now match between the two components. `border-hover` moves stone-400 -> stone-500 (Button/Outline's Hover stroke, fill_974f0cf9/#79716B in the fetched node) — this is exactly Input-field's existing `border-input-hover` value, so that token is deleted and InputField.tsx now reads the shared `border-hover`; its dark pairing (stone-400) is carried over unchanged from the deleted token, not re-derived. `border-active` moves stone-700 -> stone-800 (Button/Outline's Active stroke, #292524 in the fetched node) — Button-only; Input-field's Active (stone-600) still does not match this, so `border-input-active` is kept as the one remaining, deliberately-flagged divergence (see docs/design-tokens.md open question 1). A new `border-selected` token (stone-400, fill_5bc671a0/#A6A09B in Button's fetched node) is added: Outline's Selected state gained a border change for the first time since #56 (previously 'border unchanged, text -> text'), and this same stone-400 value is exactly Input-field's existing `border-input-selected`, so that token is deleted too and InputField.tsx now reads the shared `border-selected` on its `:focus-within` hook. `border-selected`'s dark value (stone-500) is likewise carried over unchanged from the deleted `border-input-selected` token. Note for anyone reading #56's history above: `border-selected` was removed in #56 because Selected stopped carrying any colour at all; it is legitimately back now that Figma's Outline/Selected state has a border again — this is not a mistake or a regression of #56's decision, it is a new, independently-confirmed Figma fact. `border-active`'s new dark value (stone-200, was stone-300) is this codebase's own pick, not Figma-sourced (no dark frames exist): the light value got one shade darker (700->800) so the dark counterpart was moved one shade lighter (300->200) to preserve the same relative contrast direction the token already had, consistent with how `border`/`border-hover` pair their light/dark shades on either side of the stone scale's midpoint elsewhere in this file. Button.tsx's Outline variant gains `aria-pressed:border-border-selected` for the first time, which puts Selected in direct competition with Hover/Active on `border-color` — previously impossible, since Selected touched only `text`. Verified against the compiled `pnpm ladle:build` stylesheet (documented in the PR) that hover/active still visually override Selected's border on a selected button, using compound `aria-pressed:hover:`/`aria-pressed:active:` variants (higher specificity than the plain `aria-pressed:` rule) rather than relying on Tailwind's variant emission order, which is not something this codebase controls or should assume.

duration.$comment: Ticket #86 (Sidebar collapse slide): the motion token layer this repo was missing. No Figma prototype spec exists to sync (see the primitive.duration $comment) — `base` is this codebase's own default, not a Figma-sourced value, flagged at docs/open-questions.md#sidebar-motion-timing-unsourced pending a design/product answer. `pnpm sync:tokens` emits it as `--duration-base` in app/theme.css's @theme block, giving Tailwind's `--duration-*` namespace a `duration-base` utility (Tailwind CSS v4 docs: any name works in that namespace, not just numbers). No dark-mode split applies to motion.

easing.$comment: Ticket #86, same rationale as semantic.duration above. `base` reuses the standard ease-out curve (see primitive.easing.$comment) under a project-owned name so a future retune has exactly one place to change, instead of the raw `ease-out` Tailwind utility Dropdown.tsx/ButtonToggle.tsx each already reach for directly today (their own doc comments flag this same gap — not migrated by this ticket, out of scope for a Sidebar-only fix, but a natural follow-up once this token exists).

typography.$comment: Figma text styles are Tailwind-native; no CSS generation needed. This is the authoritative mapping for agents (font: Inter).
